components.html:
The purpose of this Knit-Along is to help you get practice in shaping necklines BEFORE you knit a sweater.
The best way gain confidence is to practice different shaping methods. There is no one "perfect" solution. Your stitch pattern plays a big role in deciding which method to use.
The time spent practicing will go a long way towards success with your knitting. Beautiful neckline shaping leads helps make adding neckbands easier.
Beautiful necklines can be the difference between hand-made and home-made.

The Knit-Along is self-paced and we've scheduled live events so you can meet with other knitters to share your successes and ask questions.
If you can't make it LIVE, recordings will be available here on this page and on the Knit-along home page for the Knit-along.
Submit questions in advance

components.html:
Start with one side (cardigan)

Before trying to shape a both sides of a round neckline at the same time, take time to focus only on the shaping techniques and perfecting the appearance of your neckline shaping.
1
Build your pattern
  • Following your pattern, cast on and knit a few inches (plain or in pattern)
  • Work the neckline shaping using one of the techniques (bind off, decrease, short row) or a combination of these
  • Continue to follow the pattern and scrap off, bind off or drop the shoulder stitches from the machine
2
Neckline shaping
  • Following your pattern, cast on and knit a few inches (plain or in pattern)
  • Work the neckline shaping using one of the techniques (bind off, decrease, short row) or a combination of these
  • Continue to follow the pattern and scrap off, bind off or drop the shoulder stitches from the machine
3
Shoulder Shaping
  • For shoulder shaping practice, work the different shaping techniques (bind off, decrease, short row) to shape the shoulders
  • Scrap off the shoulders
  • As you knit more swatches, practice neatly joining the shoulders from the scrapped off pieces
Are you just getting started?

Use a light color yarn Knit in Plain Stockinette
Exercises:
  1. Use binding off for shaping
  2. Use decreases for shaping
  3. Short row shape (don't forget to wrap)
Do you have some experience?

Knit in a stitch pattern (slip, tuck, fairisle) Pay attention to the end needles to keep the edges smooth
Exercises:
  1. Use binding off for shaping
  2. Use decreases for shaping
  3. Short row shape (don't forget to wrap)
Ready for a Challenge?

Try shaping a neckline on the ribber. (Flat Rib , Full Needle Rib , English Rib ,Racking )
Exercises:
  1. Use binding off for shaping
  2. Use decreases for shaping
  3. Short row shape (don't forget to wrap)

Here are 3 shaping methods you must know. Binding off and decreasing are useful when working in pattern. Knitting Lace? these may be the preferred techniques.
Even though it creates a beautiful edge, short row shaping has its limitations. Mastering (and combining) all 3 methods will go a long way towards your success in shaping necklines, no matter what pattern you are using.

components.title: Part 1: Binding off and Decreasing Methods

components.html:
"Decrease 1 stitch every other row 10 times"
But what method is best?


Explore and compare methods below. Roll over for a closer look


Simple Decrease - on the edge
Decreasing directly on the edge makes it difficult to pick up stitches for a band.
Simple Decrease - 2 stitches from the edge
Transferring with a 2 prong tool leaves a clean edge to pick up for a band
Simple Decrease - 3 stitches from the edge
Transferring with a 3 prong tool also leaves a clean edge PLUS an additional decorative column of stitches
Full Fashion Decrease - on the edge
Transferring with a 1 prong tool creates a neat edge, if left unfinished. But could be difficult to pick up along this edge for a band.
Full Fashion Decrease - 2 stitches from the edge
Transferring with a 2 prong tool leaves a clean edge PLUS an additional decorative column of stitches
Full Fashion Decrease - 3 stitches from the edge
Transferring with a 3 prong tool also leaves a clean edge PLUS 2 additional decorative columns of stitches

Check it out!


Looking closely at the knitting in the video you'll notice where the shaping section ends and the knit straight section begins is a "wonky" spot.
This stretched out section is from that last held needle and wrap being stretched as the knit-straight section is being knit.
After the knitting "rested" (and adding a little steam) the wonky spot wasn't as noticeable
A solution to this wonky spot is to scrap off the shaped stitches before knitting the knit-straight section.
This method has 2 benefits:
  1. It prevents the last held stitches and wraps from stretching out
  2. It prevents any damage from the carriage passing over the stitches in hold repeatedly
No matter what shaping method you use, there will always be a noticeable divide were the shaping ends and the straight section starts. Be aware of this and do what you can to eliminate it.

GAUGE SUGGESTIONS FOR PRACTICE:
Gauge isn't critical for knitting these samples. (but it helps)
If you don't yet know your gauge, build your pattern with these generic gauges:
Standard: 28/44 | Mid-Gauge: 18/26 | Bulky: 16/24

slides.caption: Most bodies have some slope to their shoulders.... some more than others.
Putting a square shoulder on a slope can cause fit issues
You'll notice wrinkles near the underarm
Warning! Don't try this at home
If you just make this adjustment on an existing pattern ..... the armhole may be too short AND your sleeves won't fit in the armhole.
If you just make this adjustment on an existing pattern ..... the neckline AND center front will be too long.
A well designed knitting pattern will adjust the shape of the armhole AND the shape of the sleeve cap to accommodate the shaped shoulder.
Use a knitting pattern that already has shaped shoulders.

components.html:
Use the tabs below to explore different methods for adding shaped shoulders.
  • Knit it Now Patterns
  • Commercial Patterns + Math
  • Charting Device
  • DesignaKnit

Knit it Now Dynamic Patterns offer shaped shoulder versions. If you need more shaping, think of the armhole as a block of instructions to be adjusted without changing the depth of the armhole or impacting the fit of the sleeves. Use the Magic Formula to calculate the shoulder shaping.

To add shoulder shaping to a commercial pattern, think of the armhole as a block of instructions to be adjusted without changing the depth of the armhole or impacting the fit of the sleeves.Use the Magic Formula to accurately calculate the shaping.

Using a Charting Device is probably the easiest way to add shaped shoulders ... just be sure that the armhole opening and sleeve cap match!


Explore a couple of methods of using DAK to adjust your sleeve length.

Shoulders can be shaped by binding off, decreasing or using short rows.
  1. Using the techniques practiced in Part 1 (One side shaping), use the shaped shoulder pattern piece in your practice pattern and shape a 1/2 neckline AND shoulder.
  2. Knit a 2nd shoulder using the same method reversing the shaping (knit one left and one right neckline).

Before moving forward, be sure you understand shoulder shaping

In the next section you will be shaping the neckline AND shoulder AT THE SAME TIME

Special care needs to be taken when knitting the back of a sweater or the front of a pullover. Machine knitters stop their knitting and shape each side separately. It takes focus to get it right the first time.
In this series of exercises, you will shape a shallow neckline, commonly used for the back of a sweater.
  1. Knit a shallow neckline using your preferred method (bind off, decrease or short rows) with no shoulder shaping

  2. Knit a shallow neckline using your preferred method WITH shoulder shaping

When knitting a neck opening here are 2 critical things to consider:
  1. Lifelines:
    It's sooo easy to make a mistake when shaping necklines. Add a lifeline before you start shaping. If disaster strikes you can rip back to your lifeline and start again with fewer tears.
  2. Instead of scrapping off the opposite side, many knitters will put the stitches in hold (especially when shaping shallow necklines).
    Repeatedly passing the carriage over the stitches in hold can damage the yarn on the needles. Be sure to take steps to prevent this

components.title: Joining Shoulder Seams on the Machine

components.html:
With a "normal" depth neck opening, we can't take shortcuts like the shallow neckline. We need to split the knitting, knit one side to the shoulder, then knit the 2nd side.
Putting to work all the skills you've practiced so far, moving to a deep round neckline should be easy sailing for you.
  1. Knit a deep round neckline using your preferred method (bind off, decrease or short rows) with no shoulder shaping

  2. Knit a deep round neckline using your preferred method WITH shoulder shaping

lessons.title: Center Stitches: Bind off or Scrap off?

components.html:
Which do you prefer?
The center of a round neckline has stitches that can either be bound off or scrapped off.
Is either method "right"?
Depending on your band technique and your desired results, it's your choice.
1
Scrap off the center stitches

Notice that when you pick up "live" stitches for the band, the body stitches flow neatly to the band. There is no interruption. This is especially obvious with a stockinette band or ribbing

2
Bind off the center stitches

Notice that when you pick up stitches that have been bound off there is a definite division between the band and the body of the sweater

Take control of the depth of a round neckline.
  1. No Math method with graph paper
  2. Chart a perfect neckline
